name: Frantz Fanon
role: Martinican-French psychiatrist and anticolonial theorist; FLN member in the Algerian war (1925-1961)
summary: Fanon argued that colonialism is sustained by violence and that decolonization is necessarily a violent, total transformation led by the peasant masses rather than the urban elite. He criticised the post-independence national bourgeoisie, single-party rule and leader worship, and demanded economic transformation, redistribution from former colonial powers, and Third World and African solidarity outside the cold-war blocs.

public-ownership.rationale: Said nationalization should mean placing the entire economy at the service of the nation; demanded democratic cooperatives for trade and denounced nationalization that only transfers privileges to indigenous elites.

unions-good.rationale: Praised African trade unions (UGTAN) for a national outlook that "gradually asphyxiated" colonialism; wrote warmly of union action in anticolonial struggle.

property-fundamental.rationale: Supported peasants retaking settler-held land and nationalization for the nation's benefit, so did not treat private property as nearly inviolable.

strong-leader.rationale: Criticised dependence on one leader ("the nation should not be an affair run by a big boss") and attacked calls for "a dose of dictatorship" in underdeveloped countries.

decide-locally.rationale: Called for the party to be decentralized to the limit and for the masses to run public affairs, but also condemned regionalism, federalism and separatism as threats to national unity.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Inferred: from demanding reparation and redistribution for colonial wrongs and the end of racial domination.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Held national culture to be part of the liberation struggle but warned against freezing customs and folklore.

revolution-justified.rationale: Argued that decolonization is "always a violent event" and defended the colonized masses' armed revolt against colonial rule; joined the FLN during the Algerian war.

one-party-rule.rationale: Called the single-party system of underdeveloped countries "the modern form of bourgeois dictatorship"; wanted a party that is an instrument of the people, not of government, and opposed suppression of opposition parties.

right-to-secede.rationale: Condemned tribalism-driven regionalism and separatism and Balkanization of Africa; attacked Katanga's secession as a Belgian-backed manoeuvre against a unified Congo.

political-violence-never.rationale: Rejected nonviolence as a device that serves the colonial and bourgeois elites; held that only violence ends colonial domination.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Attacked tribalism and ethnic regression in new states and described Algerian non-Muslim and non-Arab Algerians (Jews, Europeans) who joined the cause as part of the Algerian nation.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Argued Marxist analysis must be stretched for colonies, where race divides the world and the economic base is also a superstructure; yet analysed class conflict between peasantry, proletariat and bourgeoisie; points both ways.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Presented the colonized's demand as retaking land taken by settlers; claimed it as the basis of national dignity.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Wrote that colonialism and imperialism have not settled their debt once they withdraw their flags, and that moral reparation does not feed the colonized; called for redistribution of wealth.

direct-action.rationale: Held that when the masses act for themselves without waiting for the negotiating table, the nationalist parties' bargaining is overtaken; favoured mass action over compromise through party elites.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Rejected biological racism, arguing racial inferiority is socially produced (sociogeny) and that vulgar biological racism belongs to a crude phase of exploitation.

national-self-determination.rationale: Made the nation's right to independence the centre of his writing and his FLN work.

class-collaboration.rationale: Treated the national bourgeoisie as an obstacle to be brought to heel and wanted opposition parties striving for mass participation against it; not a call for partnership.

dominated-front.rationale: Stressed the common nature of the struggle of all colonized peoples and urged African and Third World solidarity against colonial powers.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Denounced the compartmentalized colonial world and apartheid in South Africa as oppression, calling South Africa one of the "citadels of colonialism".

state-class-instrument.rationale: Described the colonial state as enforcing settler domination by police and army, and the post-colonial single party as the bourgeoisie's dictatorship.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Denounced the post-independence national bourgeoisie and officials: ministers growing rich, corruption "from police to customs", leaders cut off from the people.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Argued that the individual must assume "the universalism inherent in the human condition" and rejected superiority and inferiority between peoples; demanded equal humanity for the colonized.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Treated settlement colonies such as Algeria, Kenya and South Africa as colonialism whose settlers defend their domination with violence.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Defended the colonized's violent seizure of land and power as response to colonial violence, rejecting a blanket ban on force.

vanguard-party.rationale: Stressed political education of the masses and that spontaneity has limits, but also that the party must be an instrument in the hands of the people and learn from the masses; points both ways.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Described the colonized intellectual as cut off from the people, imitating the colonizer's culture, and having to return to the masses.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Attacked the "hierarchy of cultures" as a mark of racism, while analysing cultural relativism as a later stage of racism; mixed.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Wrote that independence is not a magic ritual but a condition for mastering the material resources, and that nationalization must organize the state on a new programme of social relations, not transfer colonial privileges to a native bourgeoisie.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Wrote that the nuclear arms race should stop and the underdeveloped regions must receive generous investments and technical aid.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Said nationalization should serve the whole nation rather than transfer privilege to an elite; no explicit general theory of property.

character-from-environment.rationale: Held that alienation and the inferiority complex of the black man are socially produced (sociogeny), and that Algerian "criminal nature" was an artefact of the colonial situation.

leader-cult.rationale: Wrote that the nation should not be an affair run by a big boss and attacked governments that abdicate in favour of a leader while the people keep silent.

land-redistribution.rationale: Said the land is the colonized people's most essential value, that peasants pose liberation as taking back land from foreigners, and criticised big landowners who seize former settler farms for themselves.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Said the black man's inferiority complex arises first from economic conditions, but also that in the colonies cause is effect (you are rich because you are white); mixed.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Described radical militants driven from the towns joining the peasants and igniting insurrection, and the war itself awakening the people, while also insisting on political education of the masses; mixed emphasis.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Condemned the "civilizing mission" and assimilationist colonial rule as masking domination and violence.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Wrote that Europe was bloated by the gold and raw materials of the colonies and that the wealth of the imperialist nations is also the colonized peoples' wealth.

national-resource-control.rationale: Condemned the colonial system for extracting the colonies' wealth for the metropolis and called for the economy to serve the nation.

multipolar-world.rationale: Said the Third World must not define itself by the choice between capitalism and socialism as defined elsewhere and must not imitate Europe; opposed the cold-war bloc alignment.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Wrote that nationalism that does not become social and political consciousness leads to a dead end; tied national liberation to the needs of the mass of the people.

notes: Historical figure (died 6 December 1961); only positions stated in his writings are recorded. Inferred answers are marked in their rationales. He explicitly said the capitalism-versus-socialism choice as defined elsewhere was not the basic issue, which leaves many economic-system statements null.
